---
title: "Lab 02 — Correlation"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
congress <- read_csv("data/congress.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
congress112 <- congress %>%
  filter(congress == 112, party %in% c("Democrat", "Republican"))
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab02", title = "Correlation")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "In the 112th Congress, dwnom1 and dwnom2 are…",
  q2 = "What does a positive correlation tell you?",
  q3 = "Which sentence is acceptable?",
  q4 = "Name one reason this correlation is not a causal effect."
)
```

## What you will do

Read a correlation of two roll-call scores. Do not turn it into a cause. Then download the `.txt`.

```{r cor-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=3}
cor(congress112$dwnom1, congress112$dwnom2)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("Weakly positively associated (r is about 0.12).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Almost perfectly associated (r is about 1)."),
  answer("A causal effect of party on ideology."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Higher values on one score tend to come with higher values on the other.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Raising one score would raise the other."),
  answer("The two scores are the same variable."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("In this Congress, the two NOMINATE scores are weakly associated.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The correlation shows that dimension 1 causes dimension 2."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "No intervention, no comparison created by design.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
